messages.subject: A Question on Random Forests
parts:
I really like Random Forests, but they are temperamental.   As a little background, I take several months of transaction history and use it to project a status the next month. For this one type of model I build, RF consistently gives great results.  The problem I have, that really limits its use in a production environment, is the factors.  If the new file doesn't have the exact same factors as the training file, the model errors out.  Even if the new model has a subset of factors, the model will fail.  Also, sometimes the new file, even if it has the same factors as the original training file, will give really strange answers that are only solved when I take the training file, delete all the rows and add in the rows from the new file.

Has anyone had similar issues?  Any suggestion on workarounds besides making sure the input file has the same factors are the training file?  Is there anything in Rattle that can be used to help here, like identifying when and where there's a factor issue?  

Thanks.

messages.author: 62fd3e97d75b32af
messages.subject: Re: A Question on Random Forests
parts:
You're just scoring new data?
 
Try stacking the new data with the original training data., scoring the combined dataset, and then tossing all the records from the original training set.
 
That will ensure that all the factors found in the training set will also be found in the scoring set. It will not of course ensure that the new data doesn't have any previously unseen factor values that were not found in the training dataset.
 
Depending on how much pre-processing you're doing, you might have to pre-process the new data, export it, combine it with the training data outside of Rattle, and bring the combined data back in.
 
HTH, I haven't had to do this myself.
 
d.d.
